note: Sources for web/public/data/pipeline.json, the numbers on the How it works page (scripts/export-site-data.py). Every count is read from the files named here; each stage names the code that implements it. The export fails if a guard layer's name is not in the gateway source or its denial code is not in the layer's own source file.

guard_layers.label: Allow-list
guard_layers.what: Each task is bound to the tools it may use. A call to any other tool is refused before it reaches the tool.

guard_layers.label: Contract scope
guard_layers.what: Strict argument schemas and the task contract: a permitted tool still cannot be pointed at records, people or addresses outside the task.

guard_layers.label: Exact-argument approval
guard_layers.what: Tools that change things need an approval bound to the exact arguments; a changed argument voids it.

flow.title: You press Run
flow.what: On the Live page you pick a mode, a defense, how the trick is written and which cases to run, then press Run. The page sends one request and then follows the job.

flow.title: The live service checks the request
flow.what: The service checks every limit before anything runs: the mode, the defense, the cases, the repetitions, the shared budget and your rate. A key you bring is held in memory for that run only, never stored or logged.

flow.title: The job waits its turn
flow.what: Accepted jobs join a queue. Each lane has a fixed number of workers, so one visitor cannot crowd out another.

flow.title: A worker starts the runner
flow.what: A worker starts the benchmark runner in its own process group, so it can be stopped cleanly. The runner fixes the case order and the seeds before the first call.

flow.title: The tasks are built
flow.what: Each case becomes a fresh copy of a small world: documents, contacts and records. In attack cases one document carries the hidden instruction, written in the chosen style.

flow.title: The helper thinks
flow.what: The agent reads the task and the documents and asks a language model what to do next. The model answers with tool calls. The agent never sees the guard's rules.

flow.title: Two arms, the same tasks
flow.what: Every case runs twice: once with the agent's calls going straight to the tools (the baseline), and once through the guard (the defended arm). Same task, same trick, same seed.

flow.title: The guard checks every call
flow.what: In the defended arm each call passes the guard's layers in turn. A call that fails one is refused and recorded with its reason; the agent is told it was refused.

flow.title: The tools do the work
flow.what: Calls that pass reach the tool service, which runs real tools over the case's own database, so every effect, safe or not, is recorded where the scorer can see it.

flow.title: The scorer reads what happened
flow.what: After each run the scorer reads the tool trace and the final state, not the agent's words, and records three verdicts: job done, nothing unsafe, attacker goal reached or not.

flow.title: The report comes back
flow.what: The runner writes a report of every pair with its trace, its gate decisions and a hash. The service reads it, explains any provider failure, and your page shows the result.
